solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: approaching means coming up to, so the vehicle arrives just before the pass

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
to pass on a turn is to give up your go

annotation.surface: A lorry heading up a mountain pass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Goods vehicle' reads as one phrase meaning a lorry; split it so 'Goods' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the freight a ship, plane or lorry carries is its load of goods.

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
arms are limbs, or members, so lacking them is armless

annotation.surface: A dull church congregation with empty pews.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Members' pretends to mean the congregation; the question mark flags that it means limbs.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym built from its parts: having no charm is exactly what unappealing describes.

entries.clue: Perhaps mug’s clothing sweetheart in dresses (5)

indicators.note: clothing wraps round a body, so ROB'S wraps round the letter
a heart lies at the centre, so the heart of sweet is its middle letter

blocks.note: to mug someone is one way to rob them; 's adds the S
the middle letter of swEet

annotation.surface: Someone wondering whether a mug is dressed in a lover's clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks mugging as one example of robbing, and 'sweetheart' here is the centre of 'sweet', not a lover.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to robe someone is to dress them, usually in ceremonial clothes.

entries.clue: Shock from right in power failure (7)

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so R sits within the power-failure word

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
an outage is a cut in the power supply

annotation.surface: Someone jolted when the power goes off.
annotation.walkthrough: The electrical sense of 'shock' fits the surface, but the answer is the emotional one.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: as a verb, outrage means to shock and anger deeply.

entries.clue: One buys almost neat second drink (9)

annotation.definitionNote: 'One buys' is a clause standing for the noun 'one who buys'.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: neat = PURE, minus its last letter
a chaser is a drink taken after another

annotation.surface: A bar order: a straight spirit followed by a chaser.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is the barroom word for an undiluted spirit, which keeps the whole clue at the bar.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the clause names the buying side of any sale.

indicators.note: first means at the start, so only passion's opening letter counts

blocks.note: first letter of Passion
honey is a term of endearment for a sweetheart

annotation.surface: Someone putting on a false show of passion for a lover.
annotation.walkthrough: Here 'sweetheart' means a loved one, not the heart of 'sweet' as it often does.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: a sham or counterfeit thing is not genuine.

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down and conceal, so the grass hides the evidence inside it

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
a sign is evidence of something

annotation.surface: A police informer hiding evidence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for an informer, which the surface leans on; here it is the plant.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: surrendering a post or a chess game is to quit it, give it up.

indicators.note: a support holds from below, and in a down clue below means later, so STILE follows HO

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
a stile is the vertical member of a door or window frame

annotation.surface: An MP standing up in opposition to the House.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an upstanding Member of Parliament; the member is a piece of joinery.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: views set against a plan are antagonistic to it.

indicators.note: protecting means shielding on all sides, so the bird surrounds the letter
finally means at the end, so only nest's last letter counts

blocks.note: a common songbird
last letter of nesT

annotation.surface: A bird guarding its nest to the end.
annotation.walkthrough: The bird is a very common one, and the letter slips in after its first four.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: news that catches you off guard is unexpected.

entries.clue: What goes round, up and down? (5)

annotation.definition: What goes round, up and down?

blocks.note: the surface reading: anything that spins, like a helicopter's blades
the setter's reading: in a down entry, a word that reads the same going up the grid as going down

annotation.surface: A riddle about something spinning and bobbing.
annotation.walkthrough: ROTOR spins round, and it is a palindrome, so in this down slot it reads identically upwards and downwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the rotating part of a machine goes round, and the word reads both ways.

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A spell in borstal holding someone back in life.
annotation.walkthrough: A borstal was a British detention centre for young offenders. In golf an albatross is three under par, but the figurative sense comes from The Rime of the Ancient Mariner.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the bird hung round the Mariner's neck became a byword for a burden that holds you back.

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
H for hard, as on pencils
aft means at the back, on a ship

annotation.surface: A Polish person with a small, firm bottom.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital P makes 'Pole' look like a nationality; it is a rod.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the long rod of a spear, club or cart is a pole.

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the pale sits behind the motorway

blocks.note: the M1, Britain's first motorway, written as MI
a pale is a fence stake, as in 'beyond the pale'

annotation.surface: A wan driver making an error on the motorway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pale' looks like an adjective; it is the noun for a fence post.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a clumsy error is a blunder.

blocks.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
to record items is to list them
ER, Elizabeth Regina

annotation.surface: A great recording with the band Queen that really shines.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Queen' invites the rock band; it is the monarch's cipher.
annotation.definitionFit: An archaic verb: it survives mainly in 'all that glisters is not gold', meaning glitter.

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the words hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: assEMBLE Mercedes

annotation.surface: Putting the three-pointed star badge on a Mercedes.
annotation.walkthrough: Fitting that the answer is the famous Mercedes star.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a badge carries a symbolic device.

entries.clue: Sailor saw a bit on travelling (9)

indicators.note: travelling means on the move, so the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A sailor on a voyage who has seen a little of the world.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Travelling' suits the sailor so well that it hides its job.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific rank: the bosun is a ship's petty officer, so one kind of sailor.

indicators.note: about means around, so the fish goes round the other word

blocks.note: a carp is a fish
ever = always

annotation.surface: Someone who complains constantly and gets worked up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carp' reads as the verb to grumble; it is the fish.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: frantic activity is described as if the body were running a fever.

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the sprint takes N inside it

blocks.note: hind = back, as in hind legs
a sprint is a race
N for new

annotation.surface: An athlete backing a sprinter over a new hurdle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hurdle' belongs in the athletics picture, but it is the definition, meaning an obstacle.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: any obstacle that holds you up in life is a hurdle.

blocks.note: the ante is the stake put in before a poker hand
to lope is to run with long bounding strides

annotation.surface: A gambler betting on a quick runner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bound for' looks like 'heading to'; split it, as 'bound' is a leap and 'for' only links.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the pronghorn and springbok are among the fastest land animals.

entries.clue: In earnest, and in general upright (8)

indicators.note: in means inside, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: earneST AND IN General

annotation.surface: Someone serious and generally honest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In earnest' reads as one phrase meaning seriously, and 'upright' as honest; both are decoys.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stones or passengers on their feet, not lying or sitting, are upright.

entries.clue: See old Church saint in decline (7)

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the old church saint letters sit within the decline word

blocks.note: to die away is to decline
O for old
CE, the Church of England
S for saint

annotation.surface: Watching the old church fall into decline.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like the verb, but it is the noun: a bishop's seat and the area he governs.
annotation.definitionFit: A church sense: a bishop's see is the territory under his authority.

indicators.note: on means placed against, so one drink sits right beside the other

blocks.note: nog is a strong ale, or eggnog
gin is a spirit

annotation.surface: The froth on top of a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head of drink' is the foam on a beer; 'Head' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: slang for the head, and fittingly also an old word for a small measure of drink.

entries.clue: Extravagantly perform part of lover, actually (7)

indicators.note: part of means a piece of, so the answer is a stretch of the following words

blocks.note: lOVER ACTually

annotation.surface: An actor hamming up the part of a lover.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part' belongs to the theatre scene, but here it points into the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: performing with exaggerated gestures is hamming it up.

entries.clue: Security, for example, checking iron temperature (6)

indicators.note: to check is to restrain or hold in, so SAY holds the metal and T inside it

blocks.note: say = for example
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
T for temperature

annotation.surface: A security guard testing the heat of an iron.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Checking' looks like testing; it means holding back, as in checking an advance.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: freedom from danger or harm.

blocks.note: a break is a rest
ore is rock containing minerals

annotation.surface: Breaking up aggregate so something can be rebuilt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Break' pulls towards demolition; it is a pause.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: bringing a building back to its former state means repairing it.

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the exploits word sits behind Romeo's letter

blocks.note: Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet
to exploit is to use

annotation.surface: Shakespeare's Romeo and his exploits in wooing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exploits' looks like the noun, deeds; it is the verb. The 's is 'has', a link.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: cunning tricks meant to deceive.

indicators.note: last means at the end, so only director's final letter counts

blocks.note: devoured = ate
a story is a fib
last letter of directoR

annotation.surface: A film studio snapping up a story; the director has the final say.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Studio' pulls towards film; the answer is an artist's workshop.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowing from French: the workshop of a painter or couturier.

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
vies = competes, struggles

annotation.surface: A mountaineer struggling while watching other climbers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Climbers' suggests mountaineers; the answer is a plant.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: these plants cling to walls and trees as they grow upwards.

entries.clue: Twitch from fish on slab’s top (5)

indicators.note: the top of a slab, read as a word, is its first letter
on means placed against, so the fish is put right after the S

blocks.note: first letter of Slab
hake is a sea fish

annotation.surface: A fish still twitching on the fishmonger's slab.
annotation.walkthrough: Slab is the fishmonger's counter, which keeps the picture whole.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small involuntary jerk or tremor.

annotation.definitionNote: 'Working' stands for the noun sense, as in 'in working order'.

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only its first and last letters
into means going inside, so PE is put inside the sermon word

blocks.note: ParablE with its middle removed
an oration is a formal speech, like a sermon

annotation.surface: A preacher working a parable into his sermon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Working' reads as the verb in the surface; as the definition it is the state of functioning.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun sense: a machine that is functioning is in operation.

entries.clue: Sign-off used in letter from bank (9)

blocks.note: since = from, as in 'since Monday' / 'from Monday'
to bank on someone is to depend on them

annotation.surface: The closing line of a letter from the bank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letter from bank' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'letter', and 'from' and 'bank' are the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 'Yours sincerely' is the standard closing line of a formal letter.

indicators.note: oddly means in the odd positions, so take letters one, three, five and so on

blocks.note: TeAk SeTtEe, letters 1, 3, 5, 7, 9

annotation.surface: Choosing a teak settee as a mark of good judgement in furniture.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface compliments the furniture buyer, and the answer is the compliment itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: good judgement in matters of style.
